questions.scenario: Tomorrow is your hardest Board Exam and you are feeling incredibly anxious. What is your coping mechanism?

options.text: Doing some quick Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation) or stretches to physically release the tension in your body.
Asking Mummy to brew a strong cup of Tulsi, Adrak (ginger), and Ashwagandha tea to biologically calm your nerves.
Putting on some soothing instrumental flute music and doing a 10-minute deep breathing and visualization meditation.
Creating a strict 15-minute break schedule and bribing yourself with a reward (like a chocolate) after finishing the syllabus.

questions.scenario: You wake up early and your grandparents are watching Baba Ramdev on Aastha/Sanskar TV. What's your reaction?

options.text: Actually sitting on the carpet and trying out the Kapalbhati and Anulom Vilom breathing exercises along with them.
Wondering how these specific breathing patterns biologically affect blood pressure and oxygen levels in the body.
Ignoring the TV but enjoying the peaceful, quiet morning vibe of the house with a warm cup of water.
Thinking about how massive the Patanjali empire has become just by selling natural wellness and grocery products.

questions.scenario: You get a massive pimple right before a family wedding. How do you tackle it?

options.text: Start doing specific facial yoga exercises and drinking lots of water to sweat out the impurities.
Immediately mix Haldi (turmeric), Besan (gram flour), and Neem because you know their natural antibacterial properties.
Light a scented candle, put on a soothing face mask, and try not to stress (because stress causes more breakouts!).
Look up the best natural anti-acne face wash brands and calculate if you can buy them with your monthly pocket money.

questions.scenario: Mummy finally lets you re-arrange and decorate your room. What is your top priority?

options.text: Leaving a big, empty space in the middle of the floor so you can roll out your mat to stretch or exercise freely.
Organizing a small shelf with different herbal teas, a copper water bottle, and natural essential oils.
Hanging warm fairy lights, putting up calming mandalas, and creating a super aesthetic, cozy corner with floor cushions.
Figuring out how you can upgrade your study table and bed cheaply by negotiating with the local carpenter.

questions.scenario: It's the PT (Physical Training) period in school, and the teacher asks you to lead the warm-up. How do you handle it?

options.text: Confidently jump to the front, showing everyone exactly how to stretch their hamstrings and do proper squats.
Explain to your friends why stretching the calves is scientifically important to prevent muscle cramps while running.
Ask the teacher if everyone can just close their eyes and do 5 minutes of deep breathing instead of running laps.
Organize the class into neat lines, assign group leaders, and make sure nobody tries to skip the drill.

questions.scenario: Your family goes to Rishikesh or Manali for a summer vacation. What excites you the most?

options.text: Waking up at 6 AM to trek up a steep mountain and doing stretches right next to the flowing river.
Visiting the local Ayurvedic shops to look at rare mountain herbs, raw honey, and natural Himalayan shilajit.
Sitting near a waterfall, listening to the rushing water, and feeling completely zen and spiritually connected.
Looking at the beautiful eco-resorts and wondering how much profit they make during the peak tourist season.

questions.scenario: You ate way too many spicy street Momos and now your stomach hurts horribly. How do you handle it?

options.text: Lie down and do the 'Pawanmuktasana' (wind-relieving pose) to physically fix the bloating and cramps.
Ask Mummy for Ajwain (carom seeds) and black salt because you know it naturally neutralizes stomach acid.
Put a warm water bag on your stomach, curl up with a soft blanket, and listen to a relaxing podcast to distract yourself.
Swear off street food for a week and plan exactly how you'll spend your momo-money on healthier snacks instead.

questions.scenario: You are endlessly scrolling through Instagram Reels or YouTube Shorts. Which video makes you stop and watch?

options.text: Fitness influencers showing how to master the perfect headstand (Sirsasana) or advanced flexibility stretches.
Informative videos explaining the biological benefits of drinking jeera (cumin) water or eating amla every morning.
Satisfying aesthetic videos of singing bowls, ASMR rain sounds, or perfectly organized calming bedrooms.
'Day in the Life' vlogs of successful people running their own aesthetic cafes, organic farms, or wellness businesses.

questions.scenario: Your best friend is crying over a bad breakup or low exam marks. How do you comfort them?

options.text: Force them to get out of bed and take them for a long, brisk walk to physically release some endorphins.
Make them a hot cup of chamomile or turmeric milk because it chemically lowers cortisol (the stress hormone).
Hug them, dim the lights, and just let them vent while playing a soft, comforting playlist in the background.
Take charge, tell them to stop crying over spilt milk, and help them make a solid action plan to fix the situation.

questions.scenario: It's the day after Diwali, and everyone is feeling heavy and lazy from eating too many Kaju Katlis and Laddoos.

options.text: Rolling out the yoga mat and forcing your siblings to do a 20-minute intense core-workout to burn it off.
Brewing a detox kadha (concoction) with cinnamon, cloves, and ginger to boost everybody's slow metabolism.
Ignoring the guilt, putting on some soft instrumental music, and just enjoying a slow, relaxing rest day.
Packing all the leftover sweets into neat boxes to distribute to the society guards so the temptation is finally gone.

Yoga_Instructor.title: The Movement Master (Yoga Instructor / Physical Trainer)
Yoga_Instructor.primary_match_text: You are a naturally active and disciplined person. You believe that a healthy mind lives in a healthy body, and you love moving, stretching, and pushing your physical limits.
Yoga_Instructor.day_in_the_life: Waking up before sunrise, leading a group of 50 people through complex yoga asanas, correcting their postures, and staying incredibly fit.
Yoga_Instructor.alternative_match_text: If not a Yoga Instructor, your active lifestyle makes you a perfect fit for a Sports Coach, Physiotherapist, or Fitness Influencer.
Yoga_Instructor.roadmap: 11th/12th: Any Stream (Science is helpful but not mandatory). Degree: B.Sc or BA in Yoga Therapy / Physical Education. Next Steps: Complete a globally recognized 200-hour or 500-hour Yoga Alliance Teacher Training Course (TTC).

Ayurvedic_Practitioner.title: The Natural Alchemist (Ayurvedic Practitioner / Researcher)
Ayurvedic_Practitioner.primary_match_text: You have a highly curious and analytical mind. You don't just follow remedies blindly; you want to know the 'why' behind nature, herbs, and how they biologically heal the human body.
Ayurvedic_Practitioner.day_in_the_life: Reading ancient Ayurvedic texts, examining a patient's 'Vata, Pitta, Kapha' doshas, and prescribing custom herbal medicines and dietary changes to cure chronic illnesses.
Ayurvedic_Practitioner.alternative_match_text: Your love for biology and natural remedies makes you an excellent candidate for a Nutritionist, Botanist, or Clinical Researcher.
Ayurvedic_Practitioner.roadmap: 11th/12th: Science strictly required (PCB - Physics, Chemistry, Biology). Entrance: Must clear the NEET exam. Degree: 5.5-year BAMS (Bachelor of Ayurvedic Medicine and Surgery). Next Steps: MD in Ayurveda or setup a private clinic.

Meditation_Guide.title: The Zen Creator (Sound Healing / Meditation Guide)
Meditation_Guide.primary_match_text: You are a deeply creative and empathetic soul. You naturally create peace wherever you go. You believe aesthetics, sound, and a calm environment are the best medicines for stress.
Meditation_Guide.day_in_the_life: Setting up beautiful, dim-lit rooms with scented candles, playing Tibetan singing bowls, and using your soothing voice to guide highly stressed people into deep meditation.
Meditation_Guide.alternative_match_text: Your creative and empathetic vibe would also make you an amazing Art Therapist, Psychologist, or Interior Space Designer.
Meditation_Guide.roadmap: 11th/12th: Humanities or Any Stream (Psychology is a plus). Degree: BA in Psychology or Philosophy. Next Steps: Pursue specialized diploma courses in Sound Healing, Mindfulness Coaching, or Clinical Hypnotherapy.

Wellness_Retreat_Owner.title: The Mindful Boss (Wellness Retreat Owner / Manager)
Wellness_Retreat_Owner.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader with a sharp business mind. You love the idea of wellness, but you enjoy building the systems, spaces, and businesses that provide that wellness even more.
Wellness_Retreat_Owner.day_in_the_life: Managing a luxurious eco-resort in the mountains, designing expensive detox packages, paying the yoga staff, and ensuring guests have a 5-star relaxing experience.
Wellness_Retreat_Owner.alternative_match_text: Your strong management skills mean you'd also excel as a Hospitality Manager, Healthcare Administrator, or Entrepreneur.
Wellness_Retreat_Owner.roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Any Stream. Degree: BBA, B.Com, or Bachelor of Hotel Management (BHM). Next Steps: Pursue an MBA in Hospitality Management or Entrepreneurship to learn how to scale your wellness brand.
